question: Has road safety for pedestrians in Brooklyn gotten better since 2013? Make a chart suitable for a local news story and summarize the findings.

options.metric: Annual number of pedestrians injured in police-reported crashes
options.denominator: No exposure denominator; raw annual count of pedestrian injuries
options.grouping: Brooklyn crash borough by calendar year, 2013–2025
options.reason: Injury counts capture the most frequent direct harm to pedestrians and make annual changes easy to see.
options.answer: Reported pedestrian injuries fell 22%, from 3,641 in 2013 to 2,835 in 2025; this outcome count does not measure risk per pedestrian.
options.interpretation: This answers whether the annual number of pedestrians injured in Brooklyn crashes changed, and the chart shows a 22% decline from 2013 to 2025. Injury counts are a direct, interpretable safety outcome, but this framing does not show deaths or risk adjusted for how much people walked.

options.metric: Annual number of pedestrians killed in police-reported crashes
options.denominator: No exposure denominator; raw annual count of pedestrian deaths
options.grouping: Brooklyn crash borough by calendar year, 2013–2025
options.reason: Fatalities are the most severe pedestrian outcome and can reveal a trend that injury totals alone obscure.
options.answer: Reported pedestrian deaths rose 30%, from 30 in 2013 to 39 in 2025, so safety did not improve on this severe-outcome measure.
options.interpretation: This answers whether the annual number of pedestrians killed in Brooklyn crashes changed, and the chart shows an increase from 30 to 39. Fatality counts are a direct measure of the gravest harm, but this framing excludes nonfatal injuries and does not adjust for walking volume.

options.metric: Annual pedestrian injuries plus pedestrian deaths
options.denominator: No exposure denominator; sum of reported pedestrian injuries and deaths
options.grouping: Brooklyn crash borough by calendar year, 2013–2025
options.reason: A combined casualty count gives a compact view of the total number of reported pedestrian victims across both outcome categories.
options.answer: Combined reported pedestrian injuries and deaths fell 22%, from 3,671 in 2013 to 2,874 in 2025, but the total masks the rise in deaths.
options.interpretation: This answers whether the combined annual count of pedestrians injured or killed in Brooklyn crashes changed, and it shows a 22% decline from 2013 to 2025. It is a defensible summary of the total reported pedestrian casualties, but because injuries dominate the total it can hide a different fatality trend and it is not an exposure-adjusted risk measure.

answer:
Reported pedestrian injuries in Brooklyn fell 22%, from 3,641 in 2013 to 2,835 in 2025, though these counts do not measure risk per pedestrian.
Reported pedestrian deaths rose 30%, from 30 in 2013 to 39 in 2025, so safety did not improve on this severe-outcome measure.
Combined reported pedestrian injuries and deaths fell 22%, from 3,671 in 2013 to 2,874 in 2025, but that total masks the rise in deaths.
